headline: Chip crash drags stocks into correction
context: The S&P 500 fell every day and ended 10% below its record, as chip stocks had their worst week since 2001.

fun_fact.text: The S&P 500 fell all five days this week, four of them by 1% or more. Before now, that had only happened in 1962, 1974, 1978, after 9/11 and in October 2008.

day_labels.2026-11-20: Chip crash: S&P in a correction

TSN.text: Results beat forecasts on Monday, and it expects a much smaller beef loss next year.

HRL.text: No company news. Food makers were a safe place to hide as tech crashed (Tyson +10.7%).

PANW.text: Sales jumped 39% to $3.45B, beating forecasts, and it raised its full-year outlook.

TSCO.text: No company news. Steadier, everyday-spending stocks held up as investors fled tech.

OKTA.text: Security stocks rallied after a string of outages, then on Palo Alto's strong results.

BE.text: Its fuel cells power AI data centres, so it sank in the AI sell-off, falling 15% on Friday.

MU.text: Memory chips were hit hard as chip stocks had their worst week since 2001.

NVDA.text: Sales doubled, but worries about its CEO's exit and an export probe outweighed the results.

LITE.text: Marvell is buying it with shares, so it fell with Marvell as chip stocks crashed.

FCX.text: Copper miners all slumped on Wednesday (a typical drop of 8.6%), then fell with the market.
